doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ode to 52nd Street and the guitar suite with orchestra
summary: He explains the homage to 52nd Street, the suite and Richard Evans's arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So again, along with expanding horizons, the one I'm holding now is "Ode to 52nd St." featuring "Suite for Guitar and Orchestra."
Right
So again, this is demonstrative of your exploration, continuing to be captivated by sounds. Expanding your own sonic palette. Could you talk about this project?

Well, I think it has two sections. One is popular songs, or jazz songs, and the other is the suite. I had an idea just to pay homage to that great street in New York that spawned so many great jazz players. Not spawned them but at least gave them venues to play. 52nd St was THE street in New York for a long time and represented kind of a platform on which we who came later built our careers on. It represented a certain quality level which we built our careers on so I felt I owed a debt to that street and what it represented. That’s why I wrote this thing called "Ode to 52nd St." Yeah so, for some reason it became a suite. It grew out of just a small form. It started to take on extra proportions here so it becomes a suite.

And for the orchestration, working with the orchestra--obviously you worked with other orchestras, you worked with Ray Ellis Orchestra and others. How did that come about? Who did the arranging and orchestration?
Well Richard Evans right?
He's credited with producing.
No, Richard Evans did the arranging.
The whole project? Okay.
And I think Esmund Edwards...I'm not sure who...
The liner notes aren't...
I think its Esmond Edwards probably did the producing, but I know Richard Evans and I worked hand in hand on the concept
Okay.
But basically the orchestra arrangements were by Richard Evans.
Okay, alright. Okay good. Was that a satisfying, fulfilling experience for you?
Absolutely.
'Cause we look at Guitar Forms, we look at this...
Richard to me is another great musician, a bass player, I don't know if he's still at Berklee or not. He was teaching at Berklee for a number of years.
Oh in Boston.
Boston, yeah. Great musician. We collaborated on a couple songs I think and I
really enjoyed it. He did my Christmas album as well which is a big seller, you know. So I enjoyed doing that.
